beats.narration: Your washer fluid just froze solid — and it cracked the reservoir.
beats.visualPrompt: Close-up on a windshield washer-fluid reservoir cap, frost visible on the plastic, static-mounted camera, cold blue-toned daylight; quick cut to a hairline crack visible along the reservoir's plastic seam.
beats.renderIntegrityNote: Split into two ~2s sub-shots (frosted cap, cracked seam) before real generation.

beats.narration: No spray, just a dry click. In freezing weather, that's a warning sign, not a fluke.
beats.visualPrompt: Close-up on a windshield wiper arm at rest, no fluid arc visible on the glass; cut to a windshield coated in road grime with a dry wiper streak across it, overcast winter light.
beats.renderIntegrityNote: Split into two sub-shots (wiper arm, streaked windshield) before real generation.

beats.narration: Summer-blend fluid — or plain water — can freeze solid below thirty-two degrees.
beats.visualPrompt: Macro shot of an unbranded washer-fluid jug exterior with frost and condensation beading on the plastic; cut to a close-up of a car exterior trim detail in a frigid parking lot at dusk (no readable text/logos).
beats.renderIntegrityNote: Split into two sub-shots (frosted jug, frigid exterior) before real generation.

beats.narration: Frozen fluid expands. That can crack the plastic reservoir, the pump, even the lines.
beats.visualPrompt: Macro cutaway of a cracked plastic reservoir tank removed from a vehicle, visible fracture line, resting on a clean workbench, slow push-in; cut to a close-up of a small pump component with a hairline split, sitting beside it.
beats.renderIntegrityNote: Split into two sub-shots (cracked reservoir, split pump) before real generation.

beats.narration: A winter-rated fluid, rated to negative twenty or lower, can keep that from happening.
beats.visualPrompt: A washer-fluid jug tipped on a static countertop rig, blue fluid pouring into an open reservoir cap with no hands or arms in frame, cold daylight through a garage door.

beats.narration: Worth checking before the first hard freeze. Stop by and we'll take a look. Nick's Tire & Auto.
